inputs.original_text: This wasn’t some spontaneous public reaction. Hundreds of groups, including unions and Muslim representative bodies, were involved, and the rally came just weeks before local elections. That timing looks deliberate: six months after one of Britain’s largest-ever far-right demonstrations, the same threat is being kept in the spotlight to steer the political conversation and shape voters before they reach the polls. The official framing makes it sound like a simple stand against extremism, but mass rallies can also be used to mark which views are acceptable and channel public opinion. I’d be wary of treating this as organic.
